subject: Intermittent queue drain — request to preserve logs and SLA eligibility
messages:
From: Jared Solomon <jared@clearpayments.com>
To: David Kim <david@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@clearpayments.com, Legal - ClearPay <legal@clearpayments.com>
Date: Mon, 29 Apr 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Incident 2028-04-29 — downtime window and evidence preservation request

David,

Between ~02:07Z and 02:23Z today (our logs), ClearPay saw a significant proportion of checkout requests returning 500s and client timeouts — roughly 65–75% failure for ~16 minutes. Our finance team is starting an audit and Legal is requesting Redwood preserve all raw telemetry, traces, and request bodies for the interval above (we will need these preserved until May 31).

Can you: 
- Confirm Redwood's authoritative service-impact window (start/end in UTC) for our tenant?
- Confirm whether this qualifies under Sec. 5.2 of our SLA for credit eligibility and, if so, how credits are calculated (pro-rata or flat)?
- Place a legal hold on any ephemeral log rotation or retention pruning that might remove raw traces for ClearPay between 02:00Z–03:00Z.
- Provide an ETA for the postmortem and the raw trace bundle (preferred: consolidated trace + list of request_ids).

We have attached a short list of request IDs and sample timestamps that hit 500s (request_ids.txt). Please treat this as high priority — our Q2 audit window is tight.

Thanks,
Jared
Sr. Ops, ClearPay

Attachments: request_ids.txt
From: David Kim <david@redwood.com>
To: Jared Solomon <jared@clearpayments.com>
Cc: sean_gallagher <sean@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, grace_oconnor <grace@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 29 Apr 2028 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Incident 2028-04-29 — downtime window and evidence preservation request

Jared — thank you for the heads up and for the sample request IDs. I’m escalating this immediately. Short answers up front: we will (a) preserve the raw traces and request payloads for the interval you called out until May 31, (b) verify the exact impact window and advise on SLA credit eligibility, and (c) deliver a postmortem timeline within 72 hours with a curated trace bundle.

Actions we are taking now:
- Legal hold placed on ClearPay telemetry (preservation_notice.txt attached) — no retention pruning will run on those buckets until May 31.
- SRE (cc: Sean) is pulling service traces and a filtered bundle keyed to your request_ids.
- Account and support (cc: Karthik, Grace) will coordinate credit eligibility review against the contract.

Could you confirm whether any downstream retries or third-party gateways were involved on your side during that interval? That helps isolate client-side vs. server-side failure patterns.

I’ll follow up with the preliminary impact window as soon as Sean posts the initial timeline.

— David
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

Attachments: preservation_notice.txt
From: karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: david@redwood.com, sean@redwood.com, grace@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 29 Apr 2028 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Incident 2028-04-29 — ClearPay contract notes (internal)

Internal note — relevant contract snippet for CP-1973: Sec. 5.2 states availability below 99.95% for a monthly calendar results in prorated credit up to 30% of monthly invoice for the affected service partition. ClearPay is on a committed Dedicated plan (monthly commit with burst). We should map the impact window to monthly availability math and run the pro-rata calc once Sean confirms the minutes of downtime and the classification (partial vs full service outage).

Also: legal wants the preservation notice to include hash snapshots of raw bundles and confirmation that S3 lifecycle will be disabled for the prefix. I started the internal ticket to freeze lifecycle.

Karthik
Account Lead
From: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>
To: Jared Solomon <jared@clearpayments.com>, David Kim <david@redwood.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, grace_oconnor <grace@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 29 Apr 2028 13:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Incident 2028-04-29 — preliminary findings and telemetry pointers

Jared — quick technical update from SRE. Preliminary timeline based on control-plane and per-tenant request traces:
- Start: 2028-04-29T02:07:14Z
- End: 2028-04-29T02:23:11Z

Symptom: elevated 5xx rate and client timeouts correlated with an autoscaler surge that left one GPU pool temporarily under-provisioned while the global routing layer rebalanced. We also saw increased KV cache evictions for the tenant during the window which amplified tail latencies. This matches the request IDs you provided.

What we are preserving and delivering:
- Curated trace bundle (Kibana-export) filtered for your tenant and request_ids (kibana_trace_20280429.jsonl).
- Full request metadata (headers, path, response codes) for the window.
- Hash manifest and storage snapshot references.

ETA: curated trace bundle and manifest by 2028-04-30 17:00 PDT; full postmortem with root cause analysis by 2028-05-02 EOD.

Notes on SLA classification: initial read suggests this is a degraded availability event affecting a single service partition rather than complete region outage — that will affect the prorata calculation. Karthik: I’ll hand off the exact minutes and the per-minute availability figure once I finalize the trace count.

— Sean
SRE Manager, Redwood Inference

Related link: https://kibana.redwood.example/app/discover#/clearpay-2028-04-29
Attachments: kibana_trace_20280429.jsonl
From: Jared Solomon <jared@clearpayments.com>
To: David Kim <david@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@clearpayments.com, Legal - ClearPay <legal@clearpayments.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, sean_gallagher <sean@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 30 Apr 2028 17:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Incident 2028-04-29 — confirmation and next steps

Dave/Sean/Karthik — thanks for the quick responses and for placing the preservation hold. We confirm the start/end timestamps Sean posted line up with our internal telemetry.

Two asks before we close the loop on our side: 
1) Please send the formal SLA credit calculation and a proposed credit amount (line-item: minutes of degraded availability, monthly prorata math according to Sec. 5.2) in writing. Our finance team will need that for the Q2 reconciliation.
2) Confirm the postmortem publication date (you referenced 2028-05-02 EOD) and whether the postmortem will include an action plan with timelines for the autoscaler and routing fixes.

Per Legal, the preservation hold should be formalized in writing (we received preservation_notice.txt but need a short confirmation email that lifecycle is disabled and SHA256 hashes will be provided for the artifacts). We will release the hold after May 31, 2028, unless we request an extension.

Once we have the credit proposal and the postmortem, we can route this to our CFO and close the ticket. Appreciate the fast turnaround.

— Jared
Sr. Ops, ClearPay

Attachments: contract_Sec5_2.pdf
